- **Causes:** a degraded or overloaded front-end server; a remote in another zone or region; long DNS caching pinning connections to one address
- **Verify:** report.network.remotes; `oprobe analyze RUNREF --by remote` and `--where remote=IP`
- **Knobs:** --concurrency; --tail-cut

<a id="finding-tcp_retransmits"></a>
### `tcp_retransmits` — Packets were lost while requests were in flight

The kernel's TCP statistics show retransmissions on a connection between consecutive samples, i.e. while a request was running on it. Loopback connections are not counted. *(network, usually warning)*

- **Causes:** a congested NIC, proxy or VPN; a lossy cross-region or internet link; a receive window or buffer too small for the bandwidth
- **Verify:** the finding's evidence: requests with retransmissions and the retransmitted segments; `oprobe analyze RUNREF --by conn`; compare from another host or region
- **Knobs:** --region; --proxy; --concurrency

<a id="finding-high_rtt"></a>
### `high_rtt` — The network round trip is long

The kernel-measured TCP round-trip time to the endpoint is at least 50 ms at the median; every request pays at least one round trip. *(network, usually info)*

- **Causes:** the client runs far from the bucket's region; a proxy or VPN detour
- **Verify:** report.network.tcp (round-trip time); `oprobe probe ENDPOINT`
- **Knobs:** --region; --concurrency; --proxy

<a id="finding-consumer_stall"></a>
### `consumer_stall` — Response bodies wait for the consumer

Data arrives faster than the application side consumes it; storage is not the limit. *(client, usually warning)*

- **Causes:** slow decoding or copying of downloaded data; a CPU-bound consumer
- **Verify:** report.stages.request_p99.stall_ms larger than body_ms; `oprobe analyze RUNREF --slowest 2 --by stage` (stage=stall)
- **Knobs:** --io-concurrency; --chunk-size

<a id="finding-overread"></a>
### `overread` — Downloaded bytes were never requested

Range coalescing or chunking downloaded noticeably more bytes than the application asked for, costing egress and bandwidth. *(efficiency, usually warning)*

- **Causes:** a large range_gap merging distant ranges; a chunk size larger than the reads
- **Verify:** report.bytes (overread ratio, backend bytes down)
- **Knobs:** --range-gap; --chunk-size

<a id="finding-small_objects"></a>
### `small_objects` — Small requests: round trips, not bandwidth, bound throughput

The mean request moves less than 128 KiB and most request time is spent waiting for the server's answer; throughput grows with parallelism, not bandwidth. *(bottleneck, usually info)*

- **Causes:** many small objects or small range reads; too little parallelism for the per-request latency
- **Verify:** report.apis (bytes per request) and report.stages.shares; the verification command doubles the concurrency; compare throughput
- **Knobs:** --concurrency; --range-gap; --object-size

<a id="finding-suffix_read"></a>
### `suffix_read` — Use suffix reads: saves one HEAD per file

File-scan operations issue a HEAD to learn the object size before reading the footer; a suffix range read returns the footer and the size in one request. *(efficiency, usually info)*

- **Causes:** readers that stat a file before reading its tail (Parquet/ORC footers); a reader without suffix-range support enabled
- **Verify:** report.apis: HeadObject requests close to the number of file scans; `oprobe run TARGET --preset parquet-suffix` and `oprobe compare` against the parquet preset
- **Knobs:** --preset parquet-suffix

<a id="finding-cache_opportunity"></a>
### `cache_opportunity` — The same objects are read repeatedly

Replaying the run through a 256 MiB read cache would save at least 200 requests per 1 000 operations: the working set is re-read. *(efficiency, usually info)*

- **Causes:** a skewed (zipf, hot-set) access pattern; repeated reads of the same footers or metadata
- **Verify:** the finding's predicted request savings; the verification command re-runs with `--cache 256MiB`
- **Knobs:** --cache SIZE; --access

<a id="finding-cost_hotspot"></a>
### `cost_hotspot` — One API or wasted requests dominate the bill

One API is at least 60% of the projected request spend, or at least 10% of the projected monthly bill buys nothing (failed or throttled requests, over-read egress). *(cost, usually info)*

- **Causes:** many small requests of one kind (HEAD, LIST, small GETs); throttled or failed requests that are billed anyway; over-read downloads
- **Verify:** report.cost.by_api and report.cost.waste_usd; `oprobe run TARGET --provider NAME --monthly-ops N` for your own volume
- **Knobs:** --range-gap; --chunk-size; --concurrency; --provider

<a id="finding-slow_start"></a>
### `slow_start` — The first seconds are much slower than the steady state

The start segment of the run has at least twice the median latency of the steady segment; short runs are skewed by it. *(sla, usually info)*

- **Causes:** cold connections, DNS and TLS at the start; server-side scaling or caches warming up
- **Verify:** `oprobe analyze RUNREF --by second`; the verification command re-runs with a longer `--warmup`
- **Knobs:** --warmup; --duration

<a id="finding-server_latency"></a>
### `server_latency` — Latency-bound on server time-to-first-byte

Requests spend most of their time waiting for the server's first byte; throughput scales with parallelism. *(bottleneck, usually info)*

- **Causes:** network round trips to a distant region; per-request service latency of the storage (normal for object stores); many small range reads that could be coalesced
- **Verify:** report.stages.request_p99.ttfb_ms dominates; `oprobe probe ENDPOINT` cold vs warm TTFB; re-run with higher `--concurrency` and compare throughput
- **Knobs:** --concurrency; --io-concurrency; --range-gap; --region

<a id="finding-download_bound"></a>
### `download_bound` — Bandwidth-bound on downloads

Transferring response bodies dominates; the per-stream or aggregate bandwidth is the limit. *(bottleneck, usually info)*

- **Causes:** NIC, VM or proxy bandwidth caps; cross-region or internet links; too few parallel streams for large objects
- **Verify:** report.stages.shares.download_pct is the largest share; report.summary (MiB/s) against the machine's network limit
- **Knobs:** --io-concurrency; --concurrency; --chunk-size

<a id="finding-upload_bound"></a>
### `upload_bound` — Bandwidth-bound on uploads

Sending request bodies dominates; upload bandwidth is the limit. *(bottleneck, usually info)*

- **Causes:** NIC, VM or proxy bandwidth caps; single-stream uploads of large objects
- **Verify:** report.stages.shares.upload_pct is the largest share
- **Knobs:** --io-concurrency; --chunk-size; --concurrency

<a id="finding-client_cpu"></a>
### `client_cpu` — Load generator CPU is saturated

The machine running oprobe is near its CPU limit, so measurements understate what the storage can do. *(client, usually warning)*

- **Causes:** CRC32C verification of large objects; TLS on many connections from a small machine; very small operations at high concurrency
- **Verify:** report.client (CPU use vs cores); re-run with `--no-verify` or fewer workers and compare throughput
- **Knobs:** --no-verify; --concurrency; --object-size

<a id="finding-client_overhead"></a>
### `client_overhead` — Time is spent outside network requests

Most operation time is client-side processing (signing, buffering, OpenDAL, CRC), not network requests. Reported only when nothing more specific explains the run. *(client, usually info)*

- **Causes:** in-memory or local backends (expected); tiny objects where per-operation overhead dominates
- **Verify:** report.stages.shares.client_pct is the largest share
- **Knobs:** --object-size; --no-verify

<a id="finding-local_backend"></a>
### `local_backend` — Local backend service time dominates

An in-process backend (memory, fs) is measured: results reflect local disk or memory, not network storage. *(bottleneck, usually info)*

- **Causes:** benchmarking memory:// or fs:// (expected)
- **Verify:** report.target.scheme is memory or fs

<a id="finding-cache_ineffective"></a>
### `cache_ineffective` — The read cache rarely hits

The in-memory read cache is enabled but almost every lookup misses. *(efficiency, usually info)*

- **Causes:** an access pattern with little reuse; a working set larger than the cache
- **Verify:** report.cache (lookups, hits, hit ratio)
- **Knobs:** --cache SIZE; --access zipf:1.1

<a id="finding-sla_p99"></a>
### `sla_p99` — p99 latency exceeds the SLA

An operation's p99 is above the `--p99-ms` objective. *(sla, usually warning)*

- **Causes:** queueing or throttling at this concurrency; tail latency of the service
- **Verify:** report.verbs[].latency vs report.sla.p99_ms
- **Knobs:** --p99-ms; --concurrency; oprobe tune --objective latency

<a id="finding-rate_not_sustained"></a>
### `rate_not_sustained` — The target arrival rate was not sustained

With an open-loop `--rate`, arrivals queued behind busy workers; their wait is part of the measured latency. *(client, usually warning)*

- **Causes:** too few workers (`--concurrency`) for the rate; a rate above what the target can serve
- **Verify:** report.open_loop (target vs achieved rate, missed arrivals)
- **Knobs:** --rate; --concurrency

<a id="finding-run_invalid"></a>
### `run_invalid` — The run cannot be judged on performance

No operation completed, more operations failed than the SLA allows, or the measurement window was shorter than the warmup: latency and throughput would describe failures or noise, so performance findings (latency, scaling, small objects, HTTP, cache, tail, cost) are suppressed. *(validity, usually warning)*

- **Causes:** failing requests (credentials, missing objects, an unsupported HTTP version); a measurement window shorter than the warmup
- **Verify:** report.summary.error_ratio against report.sla.max_error_ratio; report.run.window_s against report.workload.warmup_s
- **Knobs:** --duration; --warmup; --http

<a id="finding-run_partial"></a>
### `run_partial` — The run stopped early

The run was interrupted (Ctrl-C, Stop), stopped by a safety budget or by an error before its configured end (report.run.partial). Interrupted runs and windows under a second have their performance findings suppressed; a partial run is never accepted as a baseline. *(validity, usually warning)*

- **Causes:** Ctrl-C or a cancelled job; a budget (--max-requests, --max-bytes, --max-duration, --max-cost-usd)
- **Verify:** report.run.partial (reason, measured_s) and report.warnings; re-run with `oprobe run --from RUNREF`
- **Knobs:** --duration; --max-requests; --max-cost-usd

<!-- END finding-codes -->


<!-- source: docs/tuning.md -->

# Tuning

`oprobe tune` searches for the best client configuration **by measuring**, not by modelling. It
prepares the dataset once and then runs short trials (default 5 s + 1 s warmup) with different
knobs against the real target.

```bash
oprobe tune s3://bucket/oprobe --preset parquet --p99-ms 250 \
  --emit-profile tuned.toml --emit-rust storage.rs --emit-python storage.py --json tune.json
```

## Search strategy

1. **Baseline** — your current knobs.
2. **Concurrency ladder** — 2, 4, 8, … up to `--max-concurrency`. The ladder stops at the first
   trial that receives a 429/503 (the *throttling ceiling*), violates the SLA, or stops improving
   (two consecutive steps below +5 %).
3. **Ceiling refinement** — binary search between the last clean level and the ceiling.
   After every throttled trial the tuner pauses (`--cooldown`, or longer if that trial received
   `Retry-After`, capped at 60 s; `Retry-After` is honored even with `--cooldown 0`) so the next
   trial is not measured against a depleted rate limiter. Ctrl-C interrupts the pause.
4. **Safety margin** — the recommended concurrency is capped at 80 % of the ceiling to leave
   headroom for production variance (a trial at the cap is run when the best clean trial lies
   above it). The notes state the ceiling once — the throttled level the bisection ended on and
   the highest clean level — and explain the margin with numbers, e.g. "concurrency 12 was clean
   and measured +21 % but sits only 8 % below the ceiling, so it was not recommended".
5. **Workload-specific knobs** — coordinate descent over only the knobs that matter for the mix:
   `chunk_size` and `io_concurrency` for multipart writes and large reads, `range_gap` for vectored
   (Parquet) reads, the read cache for skewed access (or uniform access over your real objects with
   `existing_prefix` when they fit), and HTTP/1.1 vs HTTP/2 for HTTPS. A cache win that relies on
   the whole generated test dataset fitting in the cache is flagged as dataset-size-dependent.
   A change is accepted only if it improves the objective by more than 3 % (noise guard).
   For multipart writes, chunk candidates are clamped to the service's part-size limits first
   (OpenDAL raises a write chunk to `write_multi_min_size`, 5 MiB on S3/GCS), so the tuner never
   recommends a chunk OpenDAL would not use. Every report records the chunk that was actually
   written with under `effective_knobs` (requested vs effective) and warns when they differ.
6. **Confirmation** — the winner runs again for twice the trial duration; the report you get is
   from that run.

A trial is *feasible* when its error rate, throttle rate and worst per-operation p99 satisfy
`[sla]`. Infeasible trials are never chosen if a feasible one exists. If none is feasible, the
tuner reports "no trial met the SLA" and picks the least-bad trial (not throttled if possible,
then the lowest error rate). The objective throughput counts successful operations only.

## Objectives

| `--objective` | Picks |
|---|---|
| `throughput` (default) | highest MiB/s (or ops/s for small-object workloads) |
| `latency` | lowest worst-case p99 among configs within 80 % of the best throughput |
| `cost` | lowest cost per million operations among configs within 80 % of the best throughput |

## Outputs

* `--emit-profile` — your profile with the winning `[knobs]`; run it with `oprobe run --profile`.
* `--emit-rust` — an OpenDAL 0.59 `Operator` builder that reproduces exactly the measured client:
  `TimeoutLayer` (operation + I/O timeout), `TailCutLayer` (when enabled) and `RetryLayer`
  (jittered exponential backoff, 50 ms – 5 s) with the parameters oprobe applied, an HTTP
  concurrency limit only when `max_inflight_requests` was set, a custom reqwest client only when
  the knobs changed OpenDAL's default one (keep-alive off, HTTP/2), and reader/writer helpers with
  the tuned chunk/gap/concurrency (the writer chunk is the part size OpenDAL actually used). Both
  the measured operator and the generated code are derived from one `ClientStack` value, and a
  test rebuilds the layers from the generated source and compares them parameter for parameter.
* `--emit-python` — the same for the `opendal` Python package where the binding allows
  (`RetryLayer` with identical parameters); measured layers the binding cannot express (timeouts,
  tail cut, HTTP limit) are listed in the header instead of being approximated.
* `--json` — the full report of the confirmation run plus every trial (`tune.trials`).

With the default text format, everything that is part of the result — the trial table, the
recommendation and the confirmation report — goes to stdout; stderr only carries progress
(dataset upload, cool-down pauses). With `-o json|md`, stdout holds only that
document and the trial table is shown on stderr as progress.

## Budget

`--max-trials` (default 24) bounds the number of trials (the final confirmation run comes on
top); with 5 s trials the typical run takes
1–3 minutes. Use `--trial-duration 15s` for noisy networks. Every trial uses the same dataset;
the test data is removed at the end.


<!-- source: docs/cost.md -->

# Cost model

oprobe prices **what it measured**, scaled to the volume you declare. No traffic model is assumed.

1. **Per-operation usage** from the measurement window: backend requests per logical operation
   by billing class, bytes downloaded and uploaded per operation, failed/throttled requests,
   over-read bytes, and GETs/bytes served by the cache.
2. **Billing class** of each request comes from the real request line:

   | Class | APIs |
   |---|---|
   | write | PutObject, CreateMultipartUpload, UploadPart, CompleteMultipartUpload, CopyObject |
   | list | ListObjects (S3 ListObjectsV2, GCS objects.list, Azure List Blobs, B2 list_file_names) |
   | read | GetObject, HeadObject, other GETs |
   | delete | DeleteObject(s), AbortMultipartUpload |
   | free | control-plane calls (e.g. B2 authorize / get_upload_url) |

3. **Projection**: `monthly cost = per-op usage × [cost].monthly_ops × prices + stored GB × storage price`.
   Internet egress applies only to the `egress_fraction` of downloaded bytes (default 0: compute
   in the same region).

## When cost is projected

A price table is applied only when it is known to be the right one:

* the endpoint is a recognised cloud storage endpoint (`*.amazonaws.com`,
  `storage.googleapis.com`, `*.blob.core.windows.net`, `*.r2.cloudflarestorage.com`,
  `*.backblazeb2.com`, `*.aliyuncs.com`, or the scheme's implied endpoint for `gcs`, `azblob`,
  `oss`, `b2`), or
* the profile chose one explicitly (`[cost].provider` / `--provider`, or `[cost.pricing]`).

Everything else — `memory://`, `fs://`, localhost, private addresses, MinIO, Ceph or any unknown
endpoint — gets no projection: the report's `cost.applicable` is `false` with a
`not_applicable_reason`, the terminal report omits the COST section, `oprobe compare` skips the cost
check, and `oprobe tune --objective cost` refuses to run. The measured per-operation usage
(`cost.per_op`) is still reported.

## Price presets (list prices, as of 2025-06)

| Key | Storage $/GB-mo | Write $/M | List $/M | Read $/M | Egress $/GB |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `aws-s3` | 0.023 | 5.00 | 5.00 | 0.40 | 0.09 |
| `gcs` | 0.020 | 5.00 | 5.00 | 0.40 | 0.12 |
| `azure-blob` | 0.0184 | 6.50 | 6.50 | 0.50 | 0.087 |
| `cloudflare-r2` | 0.015 | 4.50 | 4.50 | 0.36 | 0 |
| `backblaze-b2` | 0.006 | 0 | 4.00 | 0.40 | 0.01 |
| `aliyun-oss` | 0.017 | 1.00 | 1.00 | 1.00 | 0.074 |

Prices change and differ by region, tier and contract: override them.

```toml
[cost]
monthly_ops = 250000000
stored_gib = 20480
egress_fraction = 0.1

[cost.pricing]
provider = "S3 (our EDP rate)"
storage_gb_month = 0.018
write_per_million = 4.0
list_per_million = 4.0
read_per_million = 0.32
egress_per_gb = 0.05
```

## Waste and savings

* **failed/throttled requests** — requests that returned 429/503/5xx/4xx (except 404) or failed on
  the network, priced at the average request price; most providers bill them and they add no value.
* **over-read egress** — bytes downloaded but not requested (range coalescing, chunked reads).
* **cache savings** — GETs and bytes the local cache answered instead of the backend.

The comparison table applies the same measured usage to every preset, answering "what would this
exact workload cost on R2 / GCS / B2?". Latency and throughput of other providers are not implied —
measure them with `oprobe run` against each provider.


<!-- source: docs/install.md -->

# Installing oprobe

## Quick

| Platform | Command |
|---|---|
| macOS, Linux | `curl -fsSL https://github.com/hxddh/oprobe/releases/latest/download/install.sh \| sh` |
| Homebrew | `brew install hxddh/tap/oprobe` (the app: `brew install --cask hxddh/tap/oprobe-app`) |
| Windows | `irm https://github.com/hxddh/oprobe/releases/latest/download/install.ps1 \| iex`, or the `.msi` |
| Windows, Scoop | `scoop bucket add hxddh https://github.com/hxddh/scoop-bucket` then `scoop install oprobe` |
| Windows, winget | `winget install hxddh.oprobe` — only once the package is accepted into winget-pkgs ([below](#windows)) |
| Rust ≥ 1.97 | `cargo install oprobe --locked` (`--features gui` adds the window on Linux; needs `libgtk-4-dev`) |

Then try it with no account: `oprobe demo` ([getting started](getting-started.md)).

### The install scripts

`install.sh` and `install.ps1` download the archive for your platform, verify it against `SHA256SUMS` and
install `oprobe` (Linux and macOS: `~/.local/bin`; Windows: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\oprobe`). Update later
with `oprobe self-update`.

They find the latest version without the rate-limited GitHub API when they can, trying in order and falling
back on any failure: the release's `latest.json`, the `releases/latest` redirect, then the API.

| Variable | Effect |
|---|---|
| `OPROBE_VERSION=4.0.0` | install this version instead of the latest |
| `OPROBE_INSTALL_DIR=DIR` | install somewhere else |
| `OPROBE_MODIFY_PATH=1` / `0` | add the directory to `PATH` without asking / never touch `PATH` |
| `OPROBE_RELEASE_BASE=URL` | release download base (mirrors, tests; default `https://github.com/hxddh/oprobe/releases`) |

**PATH.** When the install directory is not on `PATH`, `install.sh` offers to append it to your shell's rc
file: `~/.zshrc` (zsh), `~/.bashrc` (bash; `~/.bash_profile` on macOS), `~/.config/fish/config.fish` (fish),
else `~/.profile`. Piped from `curl`, the script asks on the terminal (`/dev/tty`) when there is one; without
a terminal (CI, `docker build`) it changes nothing and prints the line to add, unless `OPROBE_MODIFY_PATH=1`.
`install.ps1` adds its directory to the user `PATH` and to the current session's `$env:Path`, so `oprobe`
works in the same window (`OPROBE_MODIFY_PATH=0` to skip). It detects ARM64 Windows from the OS (also under
x64 emulation) and installs the native ARM64 build.

## Release assets

Every release publishes the same program in each platform's native format:

| Asset | Platform |
|---|---|
| `oprobe-<ver>-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz` / `aarch64-…-musl` | Linux, static (any distribution) |
| `oprobe-<ver>-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz` / `aarch64-…-gnu` | Linux, glibc ≥ 2.35 |
| `oprobe_<ver>-1_amd64.deb` / `_arm64.deb` | Debian, Ubuntu |
| `oprobe-<ver>-1.x86_64.rpm` / `.aarch64.rpm` | Fedora, RHEL, SUSE |
| `oprobe-desktop-<ver>-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz` | Linux with the window (GTK 4.14+; `install.sh`, `.desktop` entry, icon) |
| `oprobe-<ver>-universal-apple-darwin.tar.gz` | macOS (Apple Silicon + Intel) |
| `oprobe-<ver>-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz` / `x86_64-apple-darwin` | macOS single-architecture |
| `oprobe-<ver>-macos-universal.pkg` | macOS installer: `/usr/local/bin/oprobe`, man page, zsh completion |
| `oprobe-<ver>-macos-universal.dmg` | macOS app: `oprobe.app` (same binary as the `.pkg`) |
| `oprobe-<ver>-x64.msi` / `-arm64.msi` | Windows installer: `PATH`, Start menu entry, removable in *Apps* |
| `oprobe-<ver>-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip` / `aarch64-…` | Windows portable |
| `oprobe.rb` / `oprobe-app.rb` | Homebrew formula `oprobe` (CLI) and cask `oprobe-app` (`oprobe.app` from the `.dmg`) |
| `oprobe.json` | Scoop manifest |
| `winget-manifests.zip` | winget manifests (version, installer, locale) for the `.msi` |
| `latest.json` | machine-readable index: version, every asset's URL, size and SHA-256 |
| `install.sh` / `install.ps1` | the install scripts |
| `SHA256SUMS` | checksums of every asset |

Every build has the CLI and the terminal workbench (`oprobe top`). macOS and Windows builds also open the native
window (`oprobe gui`); the Linux `.deb`, `.rpm` and plain archives are headless (no GTK needed). Archives contain
`oprobe` (`oprobe.exe`), `README.md`, `LICENSE`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `man/`, `completions/` (bash, zsh, fish,
PowerShell, elvish), `profiles/` and `docs/`.

## Homebrew

The `hxddh/homebrew-tap` tap (`github.com/hxddh/homebrew-tap`) is updated by the release workflow:

```bash
brew install hxddh/tap/oprobe               # the command line (macOS and Linux)
brew install --cask hxddh/tap/oprobe-app    # oprobe.app, the native window (macOS)
```

Update with `brew upgrade oprobe` (`brew upgrade --cask oprobe-app`). The formula and the cask have different
names, so both can be installed. Each release also attaches them (`oprobe.rb`, `oprobe-app.rb`), for a
local tap if you cannot use this one.

## Windows

```powershell
irm https://github.com/hxddh/oprobe/releases/latest/download/install.ps1 | iex   # no admin rights
scoop bucket add hxddh https://github.com/hxddh/scoop-bucket; scoop install oprobe
```

The `.msi` installs for all users (Start menu entry, `PATH`, removable in *Apps*).

**winget:** each release opens a pull request to [winget-pkgs](https://github.com/microsoft/winget-pkgs);
`winget install hxddh.oprobe` works only after Microsoft's review accepts the package. Until then (check with
`winget search hxddh.oprobe`), use one of the commands above or the `.msi`.

## Debian, Ubuntu, Fedora

```bash
sudo apt install ./oprobe_<ver>-1_amd64.deb
sudo dnf install ./oprobe-<ver>-1.x86_64.rpm
```

## From source

```bash
cargo install oprobe --locked
cargo install oprobe --locked --features gui
cargo install --locked --git https://github.com/hxddh/oprobe --tag v4.0.0 oprobe
```

## Updating

`oprobe self-update` finds the release (the release's `latest.json` first, then the GitHub API), downloads
the archive for this platform, verifies its SHA-256 (from `latest.json`, or the release's `SHA256SUMS`),
checks that the new binary starts, and replaces the running one in place (`oprobe self-update --check` only
reports; `--to v4.0.1` picks a release; `-o json` for scripts). A GitHub refusal (403, rate limit) is a
network error (`net.unreachable`, retryable): set `GITHUB_TOKEN` or retry later. When
oprobe was installed by a package manager (Homebrew, apt/dnf, the `.pkg` or `.app`, Scoop, winget, the MSI,
cargo), it refuses and prints that manager's update command instead.

`SHA256SUMS` comes from the same GitHub release as the archive, so the check proves the download is
intact, not who built it: oprobe releases are not code-signed (no signing certificates), and the
checksums are as trustworthy as the GitHub release itself. `OPROBE_RELEASE_BASE` replaces the release
download base (default `https://github.com/hxddh/oprobe/releases`) and `OPROBE_UPDATE_API` the GitHub API base
(default `https://api.github.com`; set alone, `latest.json` is not fetched from github.com). They exist for
internal mirrors and tests — point them only at a server you trust, since they decide which binary is
installed.

## Verifying downloads

The checksums detect corrupted or truncated downloads; they are not a signature (see above).

```bash
sha256sum --ignore-missing -c SHA256SUMS                    # Linux
shasum -a 256 --ignore-missing -c SHA256SUMS                # macOS
Get-FileHash oprobe-4.0.0-x64.msi -Algorithm SHA256          # Windows
```

Every asset also has a [SLSA build provenance](https://slsa.dev/) attestation signed by GitHub Actions, which
proves it was built by this repository's release workflow from a given commit:

```bash
gh attestation verify oprobe-4.0.0-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz --repo hxddh/oprobe
```

## First open of unsigned packages

The project has no Apple or Microsoft code-signing certificate, so the `.pkg`, `.dmg` and `.msi` are **not
signed or notarized**. The operating system asks for one confirmation the first time:

- **macOS 15 (Sequoia) and later**: open `oprobe.app` (or the `.pkg`) once and close the warning; then open
  *System Settings → Privacy & Security*, scroll to the message about oprobe, click **Open Anyway** and
  confirm with your password. (Right-click → *Open* no longer skips the check on macOS 15.)
- **macOS 14 and earlier**: right-click `oprobe.app` → *Open* → *Open*.
- **Either, from a terminal**: `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/oprobe.app`.
- **Windows**: SmartScreen says "Windows protected your PC": click **More info** → **Run anyway**.

Homebrew, Scoop, winget, the install scripts, `cargo install` and the plain archives used from a terminal are
not affected. Verify the download (above) before you confirm.

## Shell completions (archives)

```bash
cp completions/oprobe.bash ~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions/oprobe   # bash
cp completions/_oprobe ~/.zfunc/                                               # zsh (a directory in $fpath)
cp completions/oprobe.fish ~/.config/fish/completions/                         # fish
. ./_oprobe.ps1                                                                # PowerShell ($PROFILE)
```

Packages (deb, rpm, pkg, Homebrew) install completions and man pages themselves. `oprobe completions SHELL`
and `oprobe man` generate them on any install.


<!-- source: docs/troubleshooting.md -->

# Troubleshooting

Start with the doctor:

```bash
oprobe target test prod            # a configured target
oprobe doctor s3://bucket/prefix   # any URL
```

It checks configuration, credentials, the network path (DNS, proxy, TCP, TLS, HTTP), clock skew and
list permission and a sample of the objects, and prints a summarized cause and a fix for each failure
(`-v` adds the raw backend error). It never writes unless you pass `--write-probe`, which also tests
write/read/stat/delete. Every error of every command carries a stable code (`-o json`: `error.code`)
and usually a `hint:` line.

## Errors

| Code / symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `usage.unknown_target` | the name is not in the config file | `oprobe target list`; pass a URL; `oprobe target add NAME URL` |
| `usage.unknown_run` | no run matches the RUNREF | `oprobe runs list`; use more characters of the id |
| `usage.unknown_baseline` | no baseline has that name | `oprobe baseline list`; `oprobe baseline set NAME RUNREF…` |
| `config.invalid`, `config.unknown_option` | a typo in the config file or an option the service ignores | `oprobe config edit` (validated on save); the error names the closest valid option |
| `auth.no_credentials`, `auth.denied`, `AccessDenied`, `SignatureDoesNotMatch` | missing or wrong credentials, IAM | `--credentials profile:NAME`, export `AWS_*` / `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` / `AZURE_STORAGE_*`; oprobe needs list/read/write/delete on the prefix — or measure read-only with `--existing PREFIX`, or `--anonymous` for public buckets |
| `net.tls`, `invalid peer certificate: UnknownIssuer` | private CA or a TLS-inspecting proxy | `--ca-cert corp.pem` (or `SSL_CERT_FILE`); `--insecure` for development endpoints only |
| `net.dns`, `no addresses` | wrong endpoint, or a network where only the proxy resolves names | check `--endpoint`; set `HTTPS_PROXY` |
| `net.unreachable`, `connection refused` | nothing listening | check the endpoint and port; is MinIO / `oprobe lab` running? |
| `proxy refused CONNECT` | egress proxy policy or credentials | check `HTTPS_PROXY` (with `user:pass@`), `NO_PROXY`, or `--proxy none` |
| `RequestTimeTooSkewed` | local clock off by > 15 min | enable NTP; `oprobe doctor` shows the skew |
| `PermanentRedirect`, `AuthorizationHeaderMalformed`, `region is missing` | wrong region | `--region` or `AWS_REGION`; R2 uses `auto` |
| `storage.throttled`, many 429 / 503 SlowDown | rate limiting | lower `-c` / `--max-inflight`, or `oprobe tune` |
| `safety.read_only` (exit 5) | a write under `--read-only` / `--existing` | drop the flag, or use a read-only preset |
| `safety.budget_exceeded` (exit 4) | a budget stopped the run | raise `--max-*`; the partial run is saved |
| exit 3 after a run | the SLA was breached (> 1% failed operations or corrupted data by default) or `--fail-on` matched | read the findings; `--sla none` reports without failing |

## Situations

| Situation | What to do |
|---|---|
| leftover `oprobe-run-*` prefixes | a run was killed (second Ctrl-C, OOM, power loss): `oprobe cleanup TARGET` lists them, `oprobe cleanup TARGET --yes` deletes them |
| "client processing-bound" on a remote store | client CPU, CRC verification or tiny objects: check `client cpu` in `runs show --detail`; `--no-verify`; larger objects |
| `oprobe run` asks questions in a script | it never does: prompts appear only on an interactive terminal with text output; pass a target, or `--non-interactive` |
| `oprobe top` fails in CI | it needs an interactive terminal; use `oprobe run` |
| `cannot open a window` / `built without native windows` | Linux server packages are headless: `oprobe top`, the `oprobe-desktop` tarball, or `cargo install oprobe --features gui` |
| `runs open` says no display | over SSH: `oprobe runs show RUNREF`, or `oprobe top --open FILE` in the terminal |
| `config edit` opens the wrong editor | set `VISUAL` or `EDITOR` (`export EDITOR="code -w"`) |
| `self-update` refuses | oprobe was installed by a package manager; the message names its update command (`brew upgrade oprobe`, `winget upgrade hxddh.oprobe`, …) |
| `self-update` rate limited (`net.unreachable`) | GitHub refused the request (403/429): `self-update` reads the release's `latest.json` first, so this means both it and the API were refused; wait or set `GITHUB_TOKEN` |
| macOS: "cannot be opened because the developer cannot be verified" / Windows SmartScreen | the packages are unsigned: [first open](install.md#first-open-of-unsigned-packages) |

## Error codes

Every error carries one of these codes (`-o json`: `error.code`, plus `error.docs` linking here).
The exit code follows the code's class: `2` usage/config, `1` runtime, `3` gate, `4` budget,
`5` safety refusal, `130` interrupted.

<a id="usage-invalid_argument"></a>
### `usage.invalid_argument` (exit 2)

A flag, argument or tool input is malformed: an unknown flag, a value that does not parse
(`--max-bytes lots`), an output format the command does not have (`-o html` where there is no
HTML renderer). With `-o json|ndjson` argument errors are JSON too. Fix the argument; `--help`
lists what the command accepts.

<a id="usage-unknown_target"></a>
### `usage.unknown_target` (exit 2)

The target name is not in the config file, or no target was given. `oprobe target list`; pass a
URL (`s3://bucket/prefix`, `memory://`); `oprobe target add NAME URL`.

<a id="usage-unknown_run"></a>
### `usage.unknown_run` (exit 2)

No stored run matches the RUNREF. `oprobe runs list`; use more characters of the id, `last`,
`last~N`, a label or a path to a `.oprobe` file.

<a id="usage-unknown_baseline"></a>
### `usage.unknown_baseline` (exit 2)

No baseline has that name. `oprobe baseline list`; create one with `oprobe baseline set NAME
RUNREF…` or `oprobe run … --baseline NAME`.

<a id="config-invalid"></a>
### `config.invalid` (exit 2)

The config file (or a profile) does not parse or has an invalid value, e.g. an unknown key under
`[defaults]` or `[defaults.budgets]`. `oprobe config edit` validates on save; `oprobe config show`
prints every effective value and its source.

<a id="config-unknown_option"></a>
### `config.unknown_option` (exit 2)

A backend option the service does not know (`--option`, `[targets.NAME.options]`). The message
names the closest valid option.

<a id="auth-no_credentials"></a>
### `auth.no_credentials` (exit 1)

No credentials were found. Export the provider's variables (`AWS_*`,
`GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS`, `AZURE_STORAGE_*`), set `credentials = "profile:NAME"` on the
target, or use `--anonymous` for public buckets.

<a id="auth-denied"></a>
### `auth.denied` (exit 1)

The service refused the credentials or the operation (`AccessDenied`, `SignatureDoesNotMatch`,
403). oprobe needs list/read/write/delete on the prefix; measure read-only with
`--existing PREFIX`. `oprobe doctor TARGET` checks each permission.

<a id="net-unreachable"></a>
### `net.unreachable` (exit 1, retryable)

Nothing answered (`connection refused`, reset, no route). Check the endpoint and port; is MinIO /
`oprobe lab` running? Behind an egress proxy check `HTTPS_PROXY` / `NO_PROXY` or `--proxy none`.

<a id="net-dns"></a>
### `net.dns` (exit 1, retryable)

The endpoint's name did not resolve. Check `--endpoint`; on networks where only the proxy
resolves names set `HTTPS_PROXY`.

<a id="net-tls"></a>
### `net.tls` (exit 1)

The TLS handshake failed (`invalid peer certificate: UnknownIssuer`, expired or mismatched
certificate): a private CA or a TLS-inspecting proxy. `--ca-cert corp.pem` (or `SSL_CERT_FILE`);
`--insecure` for development endpoints only.

<a id="net-timeout"></a>
### `net.timeout` (exit 1, retryable)

A request or connection timed out. Check the network path with `oprobe doctor`; lower the
concurrency if the client or the link is saturated.

<a id="net-rate_limited"></a>
### `net.rate_limited` (exit 1, retryable)

An HTTP API other than the storage target (GitHub releases for `oprobe self-update`, an OTLP
collector) refused the request because its rate limit is exhausted (429, or 403 with no quota
left). Wait and retry; for GitHub, set `GITHUB_TOKEN` to raise the limit. Your storage
credentials are not involved.

<a id="net-http"></a>
### `net.http` (exit 1)

An HTTP API other than the storage target answered with an error (for example GitHub 403 or 404
for a release, or an OTLP collector rejecting a push). The message names the URL and the status.
Check the URL, the release tag or the collector; your storage credentials are not involved.

<a id="storage-not_found"></a>
### `storage.not_found` (exit 1)

The bucket, container, root or `--existing` prefix does not exist, or holds no objects. Check the
URL and region; with `--existing PREFIX` list the prefix first.

<a id="storage-throttled"></a>
### `storage.throttled` (exit 1, retryable)

The service rate-limited the requests (429, 503 SlowDown). Lower `-c` / `--max-inflight`, or let
`oprobe tune` find the limit.

<a id="storage-unsupported"></a>
### `storage.unsupported` (exit 1)

The service does not support an operation the workload needs (e.g. multipart, copy, presign).
Pick another preset; `oprobe doctor` prints the service's capability matrix.

<a id="safety-budget_exceeded"></a>
### `safety.budget_exceeded` (exit 4)

A budget (`--max-cost-usd`, `--max-requests`, `--max-bytes`, `--max-duration`, or
`[defaults.budgets]`) stopped the command. Budgets cover the whole command: every run of
`run --repeat`, every cell of `matrix`, every window of `watch`. The partial run is saved and
test data cleaned up. Raise the budget or shorten the run; `--dry-run` shows the estimates.

<a id="safety-read_only"></a>
### `safety.read_only` (exit 5)

The command would write or delete under `--read-only` / `--existing`, or on a read-only MCP
server. Drop the flag, benchmark existing objects with `--existing PREFIX`, or start the MCP
server with `--allow-write`.

<a id="safety-refused"></a>
### `safety.refused` (exit 5)

A safety rail refused the command: a target outside the MCP server's `--allow-target` list (or a
call that overrides the endpoint, bucket, root, proxy or TLS settings of an allowed target), or
`oprobe mcp --http` on a non-loopback address without `--http-allow-remote`.

<a id="run-sla_failed"></a>
### `run.sla_failed` (exit 3)

The run breached its SLA (by default > 1% failed operations or corrupted data) or `--fail-on`
matched. Read the findings; `--sla none` reports without failing.

<a id="run-regression"></a>
### `run.regression` (exit 3)

`oprobe compare` (or `run --baseline`) found a significant regression against the baseline.
`oprobe compare A B` shows each check; see [CI](ci.md) for thresholds.

<a id="run-interrupted"></a>
### `run.interrupted` (exit 130, retryable)

Ctrl-C, Stop or `cancel_run` ended the command. Test data was cleaned up unless Ctrl-C was
pressed twice (then `oprobe cleanup TARGET`). Run it again.

<a id="internal"></a>
### `internal` (exit 1)

An unexpected failure. Rerun with the same arguments; if it persists, report it with the
command line and the error message.

[Reading the report](reading-the-report.md) explains each verdict and section.


<!-- source: docs/privacy.md -->

# Privacy

**oprobe sends no telemetry.** No usage statistics, crash reports or analytics, and no setting to turn any on.

## What oprobe connects to

| When | Where |
|---|---|
| `run`, `tune`, `doctor`, `target test`, `probe`, `watch`, `matrix`, `compat`, `cleanup`, the app | the storage endpoint you give it (and your proxy, if `HTTPS_PROXY` / `--proxy` is set); credential providers of that cloud (instance metadata, STS, SSO) when the provider chain needs them |
| `demo`, `lab`, `lab://…` targets | nothing: the lab runs inside oprobe on 127.0.0.1 |
| `self-update` | GitHub's release download host (`latest.json`, the archive) and, as a fallback, `api.github.com` (set `OPROBE_RELEASE_BASE` / `OPROBE_UPDATE_API` to use a mirror) |
| the GitHub Action | GitHub (to download a pinned release and comment on the pull request) |

Nothing else. The HTML report is one self-contained file: opening it loads nothing from the network.

## What oprobe stores

- **Runs** in `<data dir>/oprobe/runs/` (`oprobe config path`): the report, the resolved configuration and one
  row per operation and request. Object keys, request IDs and remote IP addresses are part of a run; secrets
  are not: credential options (`secret_access_key`, `account_key`, `sas_token`, `password`, `*_key`, …) are
  redacted before anything is printed or saved, and URLs lose embedded credentials and query strings.
- **The host** is recorded as OS, architecture, CPU count and a hash of the host name, never the name itself.
- **The config file** holds what you put there (`oprobe target add` stores the URL, region, endpoint, the
  credential *source* such as `profile:prod`, and options — never keys unless you write them yourself).

Delete runs with `oprobe runs rm` / `oprobe runs gc`, or remove the data directory.

## Test data in your bucket

`oprobe run` writes under `<prefix>/oprobe-run-<id>/` and deletes it at the end, verifying the prefix is empty.
`--read-only` and `--existing` never write; `--dry-run` sends nothing; `oprobe doctor` writes only with
`--write-probe`. Leftovers from killed runs are listed with `oprobe cleanup TARGET` (a dry run) and
removed with `oprobe cleanup TARGET --yes`.


<!-- source: docs/cli.md -->

# CLI reference

<!-- Generated by `oprobe man --markdown` from the command definitions; do not edit by hand. Refresh: `OPROBE_BLESS=1 cargo test --test docs`. -->

oprobe drives realistic workloads through Apache OpenDAL and traces every backend request: queue wait, DNS/TCP/TLS handshakes, request send, time-to-first-byte, transfer and consumer stall. It explains the bottleneck, projects the cloud bill, tunes the client configuration and gates regressions in CI.

Every command accepts the global options below. Exit codes: `0` ok · `1` runtime failure · `2` usage/config · `3` SLA failed or regression · `4` budget exceeded · `5` safety refusal · `130` interrupted.

## Global options

| argument | description |
|---|---|
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Output format of the result on stdout (logs and progress go to stderr) · one of `text`, `json`, `ndjson`, `md`, `html` · env `OPROBE_OUTPUT` |
| `--color <COLOR>` | When to use colors · one of `auto`, `always`, `never` · default `auto` |
| `-q, --quiet` | No progress or informational messages on stderr |
| `--non-interactive` | Never prompt or redraw (implied when stdin/stdout is not a terminal) |
| `--config <PATH>` | Config file (default: $OPROBE_CONFIG or <config dir>/oprobe/config.toml) |

## Commands

| command | what it does |
|---|---|
| [`oprobe run`](#oprobe-run) | Measure a target: where time and money go (saves the run) |
| [`oprobe demo`](#oprobe-demo) | Start a lab target with throttling and stragglers, run it and narrate the result |
| [`oprobe tune`](#oprobe-tune) | Find the best client configuration for a workload (throttle-aware) |
| [`oprobe compare`](#oprobe-compare) | Regression gate: compare two runs (RUNREFs or files) and fail on regressions |
| [`oprobe verify`](#oprobe-verify) | Test a finding's advice: replay the run with and without the change (A B A B…) and answer confirmed, refuted or inconclusive |
| [`oprobe fix`](#oprobe-fix) | Diagnose a target, tune it and verify the recommendation; prints a profile patch |
| [`oprobe runs`](#oprobe-runs) | Saved runs: list, show, open, export, rm, gc |
| [`oprobe analyze`](#oprobe-analyze) | Re-slice a run by API, connection, remote, stage or second |
| [`oprobe explain`](#oprobe-explain) | Narrate a run's causes and advice, or document a finding code |
| [`oprobe target`](#oprobe-target) | Named targets: add, list, show, rm, test, discover (credential sources), sample |
| [`oprobe doctor`](#oprobe-doctor) | Check endpoint reachability, TLS, clock skew, credentials and permissions |
| [`oprobe probe`](#oprobe-probe) | Measure DNS / TCP / proxy / TLS handshakes and cold vs warm TTFB of an endpoint |
| [`oprobe watch`](#oprobe-watch) | Continuous low-rate probing with SLOs and a Prometheus endpoint |
| [`oprobe matrix`](#oprobe-matrix) | Run the same workload across targets / knob values and rank them |
| [`oprobe compat`](#oprobe-compat) | Correctness & compatibility suite for a target |
| [`oprobe baseline`](#oprobe-baseline) | Named baselines: set, list, rm, show |
| [`oprobe lab`](#oprobe-lab) | Start a local S3-compatible server with programmable faults |
| [`oprobe mcp`](#oprobe-mcp) | MCP server for agents (stdio, or --http ADDR) |
| [`oprobe schema`](#oprobe-schema) | Print the JSON Schema of a machine output (report, events, …) |
| [`oprobe capabilities`](#oprobe-capabilities) | Describe what this oprobe can do (machine-readable) |
| [`oprobe config`](#oprobe-config) | Configuration: show (with sources), path, edit |
| [`oprobe cleanup`](#oprobe-cleanup) | Remove test data left behind by interrupted runs |
| [`oprobe self-update`](#oprobe-self-update) | Check, download, verify and install the latest release |
| [`oprobe top`](#oprobe-top) | Interactive workbench in this terminal: run, tune and probe with live charts |
| [`oprobe gui`](#oprobe-gui) | The same workbench in a native window (macOS, Windows, Linux with GTK 4) |
| [`oprobe completions`](#oprobe-completions) | Generate shell completions |
| [`oprobe man`](#oprobe-man) | Generate the man page |

## `oprobe run`

Measure a target: where time and money go (saves the run)

```text
oprobe run [OPTIONS] [TARGET]
```

Output formats (`-o`): text, json, ndjson, md, html

*Target*

| argument | description |
|---|---|
| `<TARGET>` | Target name (see `oprobe target list`) or storage URL: s3://bucket/prefix, gcs://bucket, azblob://container, oss://, cos://, b2://, fs:///path, memory:// |
| `-p, --profile <FILE>` | Load a profile (TOML); flags override its values |
| `--endpoint <ENDPOINT>` | Custom endpoint (MinIO, R2, Ceph, private clouds) |
| `--region <REGION>` | Region of the bucket (e.g. us-east-1); most S3-compatible services accept any value |
| `--option <KEY=VALUE>` | Extra backend option, repeatable (e.g. --option enable_virtual_host_style=true) |
| `--anonymous` | Access a public bucket without credentials (s3, gcs, azblob, oss: unsigned requests) |
| `--ca-cert <PEM>` | Trust an extra PEM CA bundle |
| `--insecure` | Skip TLS certificate verification (development only) |
| `--proxy <PROXY>` | Egress proxy URL, or `none` to ignore HTTPS_PROXY/HTTP_PROXY |

*Workload*

| argument | description |
|---|---|
| `--preset <PRESET>` | Workload preset: parquet, checkpoint, small-files, metadata, mixed |
| `-d, --duration <DURATION>` | Measurement window (e.g. 30s, 2m) |
| `--warmup <WARMUP>` | Warmup before measuring (connections, caches) |
| `--max-ops <MAX_OPS>` | Stop after N measured operations |
| `--rate <RATE>` | Open-loop arrival rate (ops/s); latency is measured from the intended start time |
| `--existing <PREFIX>` | Benchmark existing objects under this prefix (read-only) |
| `--objects <OBJECTS>` | Number of dataset objects to generate |
| `--object-size <OBJECT_SIZE>` | Size of each generated object (e.g. 16MiB) |
| `--access <ACCESS>` | Key popularity: uniform, zipf:1.1, hotset:0.2/0.8 |
| `--persist-dataset` | Keep the generated dataset for later runs (oprobe-dataset/<fingerprint>/) |
| `--no-verify` | Skip CRC32C verification |
| `--keep-data` | Do not delete test data when the run ends |

*Client knobs*

| argument | description |
|---|---|
| `-c, --concurrency <CONCURRENCY>` | Concurrent operations (workers) |
| `--io-concurrency <IO_CONCURRENCY>` | Per-operation reader/writer parallelism |
| `--chunk-size <CHUNK_SIZE>` | Reader/writer chunk and multipart part size (e.g. 8MiB) |
| `--range-gap <RANGE_GAP>` | Merge vectored ranges closer than this (e.g. 64KiB) |
| `--max-inflight <MAX_INFLIGHT>` | Cap in-flight HTTP requests (0 = unlimited) |
| `--http <HTTP>` | HTTP version · one of `auto`, `h1`, `h2` |
| `--no-keep-alive` | Open a new connection for every request |
| `--microscope` | Use oprobe's instrumented connection pool instead of OpenDAL's own HTTP client: exact pool queueing, per-dial DNS/TCP/proxy/TLS and HTTP/2 streams, at the cost of measuring a different client than production runs |
| `--cache <SIZE>` | Enable the in-memory read cache with this size (e.g. 512MiB) |
| `--retries <RETRIES>` | Retry attempts for temporary errors |
| `--tail-cut` | Cancel and retry straggler requests (TailCutLayer) |
| `--addressing <STYLE>` | S3 bucket addressing: auto (as configured), virtual (bucket.host) or path (host/bucket) |
| `--checksum <ALGO>` | Checksum computed by the client and verified by the server on writes (S3: crc32c) |
| `--sse <MODE>` | Server-side encryption of written objects (S3: AES256, aws:kms) |

*Cost*

| argument | description |
|---|---|
| `--provider <PROVIDER>` | Pricing preset: aws-s3, gcs, azure-blob, cloudflare-r2, backblaze-b2, aliyun-oss (aliases: aws, gcp, google, azure, r2, b2, oss, aliyun) |
| `--monthly-ops <MONTHLY_OPS>` | Logical operations per month to project costs for |
| `--egress-fraction <EGRESS_FRACTION>` | Fraction of downloads leaving the cloud (0..1) |
| `--stored-gib <STORED_GIB>` | Stored data in GiB |

*SLA (exit code 3 when breached)*

| argument | description |
|---|---|
| `--sla <MODE>` | `none` reports the SLA verdict without failing the command · one of `enforce`, `none` |
| `--max-error-rate <RATE>` | Max share of failed operations, e.g. 1% or 0.01 (default 1%) |
| `--max-throttle-rate <RATE>` | Max share of throttled (429/503) operations, e.g. 0% (default: not checked by `run`; `tune` rejects any throttling) |
| `--p99-ms <MS>` | Max p99 latency per operation in ms (tune rejects trials above it) |

*Output*

| argument | description |
|---|---|
| `--json <FILE>` | Also save the report as JSON (input for `oprobe compare`) |
| `--markdown <FILE>` | Also save a Markdown report |
| `--no-save` | Do not save the run in the run store |
| `--fail-on <FAIL_ON>` | Also exit with code 3 if the diagnosis has findings of this severity or worse (SLA breaches always do, unless `--sla none`) · one of `warning`, `critical` |
| `--label <LABEL>` | Label stored in the report (e.g. a git SHA) |

*Safety*

| argument | description |
|---|---|
| `--dry-run` | Print the plan (requests, bytes, objects written/deleted, cost, ETA) and exit |
| `--read-only` | Refuse every write and delete (exit 5); implied by --existing |
| `--max-cost-usd <USD>` | Stop when the estimated request cost exceeds this (USD; exit 4) |
| `--max-requests <N>` | Stop after this many backend requests (exit 4) |
| `--max-bytes <SIZE>` | Stop after transferring this many bytes, e.g. 10GiB (exit 4) |
| `--max-duration <DURATION>` | Stop after this much wall time, e.g. 5m (exit 4) |
| `--idempotency-key <KEY>` | Name the run prefix after KEY: a retried command reuses and cleans it up |
| `--repeat <N>` | Repeat the run N times and report the spread · default `1` |
| `--baseline <NAME>` | Compare against (and add to) a named baseline |

*Replay*

| argument | description |
|---|---|
| `--from <RUNREF>` | Replay a stored run (RUNREF): its spec, with credentials resolved again from the target; other flags and --set override it |
| `--set <KEY=VALUE>` | Override one setting, repeatable (e.g. --set concurrency=8 --set warmup=1s); keys: the profile's knob, workload, SLA and cost names, `endpoint`, `region`, `label` |

## `oprobe demo`

Start a lab target with throttling and stragglers, run it and narrate the result

```text
oprobe demo [OPTIONS]
```

Output formats (`-o`): text, json, ndjson, md, html

## `oprobe tune`

Find the best client configuration for a workload (throttle-aware)

```text
oprobe tune [OPTIONS] [TARGET]
```

Output formats (`-o`): text, json, ndjson, md

*Target*

| argument | description |
|---|---|
| `<TARGET>` | Target name (see `oprobe target list`) or storage URL: s3://bucket/prefix, gcs://bucket, azblob://container, oss://, cos://, b2://, fs:///path, memory:// |
| `-p, --profile <FILE>` | Load a profile (TOML); flags override its values |
| `--endpoint <ENDPOINT>` | Custom endpoint (MinIO, R2, Ceph, private clouds) |
| `--region <REGION>` | Region of the bucket (e.g. us-east-1); most S3-compatible services accept any value |
| `--option <KEY=VALUE>` | Extra backend option, repeatable (e.g. --option enable_virtual_host_style=true) |
| `--anonymous` | Access a public bucket without credentials (s3, gcs, azblob, oss: unsigned requests) |
| `--ca-cert <PEM>` | Trust an extra PEM CA bundle |
| `--insecure` | Skip TLS certificate verification (development only) |
| `--proxy <PROXY>` | Egress proxy URL, or `none` to ignore HTTPS_PROXY/HTTP_PROXY |

*Workload*

| argument | description |
|---|---|
| `--preset <PRESET>` | Workload preset: parquet, checkpoint, small-files, metadata, mixed |
| `-d, --duration <DURATION>` | Measurement window (e.g. 30s, 2m) |
| `--warmup <WARMUP>` | Warmup before measuring (connections, caches) |
| `--max-ops <MAX_OPS>` | Stop after N measured operations |
| `--rate <RATE>` | Open-loop arrival rate (ops/s); latency is measured from the intended start time |
| `--existing <PREFIX>` | Benchmark existing objects under this prefix (read-only) |
| `--objects <OBJECTS>` | Number of dataset objects to generate |
| `--object-size <OBJECT_SIZE>` | Size of each generated object (e.g. 16MiB) |
| `--access <ACCESS>` | Key popularity: uniform, zipf:1.1, hotset:0.2/0.8 |
| `--persist-dataset` | Keep the generated dataset for later runs (oprobe-dataset/<fingerprint>/) |
| `--no-verify` | Skip CRC32C verification |
| `--keep-data` | Do not delete test data when the run ends |

*Client knobs*

| argument | description |
|---|---|
| `-c, --concurrency <CONCURRENCY>` | Concurrent operations (workers) |
| `--io-concurrency <IO_CONCURRENCY>` | Per-operation reader/writer parallelism |
| `--chunk-size <CHUNK_SIZE>` | Reader/writer chunk and multipart part size (e.g. 8MiB) |
| `--range-gap <RANGE_GAP>` | Merge vectored ranges closer than this (e.g. 64KiB) |
| `--max-inflight <MAX_INFLIGHT>` | Cap in-flight HTTP requests (0 = unlimited) |
| `--http <HTTP>` | HTTP version · one of `auto`, `h1`, `h2` |
| `--no-keep-alive` | Open a new connection for every request |
| `--microscope` | Use oprobe's instrumented connection pool instead of OpenDAL's own HTTP client: exact pool queueing, per-dial DNS/TCP/proxy/TLS and HTTP/2 streams, at the cost of measuring a different client than production runs |
| `--cache <SIZE>` | Enable the in-memory read cache with this size (e.g. 512MiB) |
| `--retries <RETRIES>` | Retry attempts for temporary errors |
| `--tail-cut` | Cancel and retry straggler requests (TailCutLayer) |
| `--addressing <STYLE>` | S3 bucket addressing: auto (as configured), virtual (bucket.host) or path (host/bucket) |
| `--checksum <ALGO>` | Checksum computed by the client and verified by the server on writes (S3: crc32c) |
| `--sse <MODE>` | Server-side encryption of written objects (S3: AES256, aws:kms) |

*Cost*

| argument | description |
|---|---|
| `--provider <PROVIDER>` | Pricing preset: aws-s3, gcs, azure-blob, cloudflare-r2, backblaze-b2, aliyun-oss (aliases: aws, gcp, google, azure, r2, b2, oss, aliyun) |
| `--monthly-ops <MONTHLY_OPS>` | Logical operations per month to project costs for |
| `--egress-fraction <EGRESS_FRACTION>` | Fraction of downloads leaving the cloud (0..1) |
| `--stored-gib <STORED_GIB>` | Stored data in GiB |

*SLA (exit code 3 when breached)*

| argument | description |
|---|---|
| `--sla <MODE>` | `none` reports the SLA verdict without failing the command · one of `enforce`, `none` |
| `--max-error-rate <RATE>` | Max share of failed operations, e.g. 1% or 0.01 (default 1%) |
| `--max-throttle-rate <RATE>` | Max share of throttled (429/503) operations, e.g. 0% (default: not checked by `run`; `tune` rejects any throttling) |
| `--p99-ms <MS>` | Max p99 latency per operation in ms (tune rejects trials above it) |

*Output*

| argument | description |
|---|---|
| `--json <FILE>` | Also save the report as JSON (input for `oprobe compare`) |
| `--markdown <FILE>` | Also save a Markdown report |
| `--no-save` | Do not save the run in the run store |
| `--fail-on <FAIL_ON>` | Also exit with code 3 if the diagnosis has findings of this severity or worse (SLA breaches always do, unless `--sla none`) · one of `warning`, `critical` |
| `--label <LABEL>` | Label stored in the report (e.g. a git SHA) |

*Safety*

| argument | description |
|---|---|
| `--dry-run` | Print the plan (requests, bytes, objects written/deleted, cost, ETA) and exit |
| `--read-only` | Refuse every write and delete (exit 5); implied by --existing |
| `--max-cost-usd <USD>` | Stop when the estimated request cost exceeds this (USD; exit 4) |
| `--max-requests <N>` | Stop after this many backend requests (exit 4) |
| `--max-bytes <SIZE>` | Stop after transferring this many bytes, e.g. 10GiB (exit 4) |
| `--max-duration <DURATION>` | Stop after this much wall time, e.g. 5m (exit 4) |
| `--idempotency-key <KEY>` | Name the run prefix after KEY: a retried command reuses and cleans it up |

*Tuning*

| argument | description |
|---|---|
| `--objective <OBJECTIVE>` | What to optimize · one of `goodput`, `p99`, `cost`, `balanced` · default `goodput` |
| `--trial-duration <TRIAL_DURATION>` | Measurement window per trial · default `5s` |
| `--trial-warmup <TRIAL_WARMUP>` | Warmup per trial · default `1s` |
| `--max-trials <MAX_TRIALS>` | Maximum number of trials · default `24` |
| `--max-concurrency <MAX_CONCURRENCY>` | Highest concurrency to try · default `256` |
| `--cooldown <COOLDOWN>` | Pause after a throttled trial · default `5s` |
| `--max-throttle-ratio <RATIO>` | Share of throttled requests a configuration may cause and still be feasible (default 0.001, or the profile's `sla.max_throttle_rate`) |
| `--boundary-repeats <BOUNDARY_REPEATS>` | Runs of each bisection trial near the throttle boundary · default `2` |
| `--headroom-ratio <RATIO>` | In-flight headroom kept below the throttling ceiling (default 0.15) |
| `--budget <DURATION>` | Total wall-time budget of the tuner, e.g. 5m: caps the trials so the estimate fits (add --max-duration for a hard stop) |
| `--emit-profile <FILE>` | Write the tuned profile (TOML) |
| `--emit-rust <FILE>` | Write a Rust/OpenDAL snippet with the tuned settings |
| `--emit-python <FILE>` | Write a Python/OpenDAL snippet with the tuned settings |

## `oprobe compare`

Regression gate: compare two runs (RUNREFs or files) and fail on regressions

```text
oprobe compare [OPTIONS] [A] [B]
```

Output formats (`-o`): text, json, ndjson, md, html

| argument | description |
|---|---|
| `<A>` | Baseline: RUNREF (id, prefix, last~N, label) or a .oprobe / report .json file |
| `<B>` | Candidate: RUNREF or file (default: `last`) |
| `--baseline <NAME>` | Compare against a named baseline instead of A |
| `--max-p99-increase <MAX_P99_INCREASE>` | Max p99 increase per operation (%) · default `20` |
| `--max-p50-increase <MAX_P50_INCREASE>` | Max p50 increase per operation (%) · default `20` |
| `--min-latency-delta-ms <MIN_LATENCY_DELTA_MS>` | Ignore latency changes smaller than this (ms) · default `1` |
| `--max-throughput-drop <MAX_THROUGHPUT_DROP>` | Max throughput drop (%) · default `10` |
| `--max-error-increase <MAX_ERROR_INCREASE>` | Max increase of failed operations (percentage points) · default `0.5` |
| `--max-request-amp-increase <MAX_REQUEST_AMP_INCREASE>` | Max increase of requests per operation (%) · default `10` |
| `--max-read-amp-increase <MAX_READ_AMP_INCREASE>` | Max increase of read amplification (%) · default `10` |
| `--max-cost-increase <MAX_COST_INCREASE>` | Max increase of cost per operation (%) · default `10` |
| `--min-samples <MIN_SAMPLES>` | Minimum samples per operation for latency checks · default `30` |
| `--allow-throttling` | Do not fail when the candidate starts getting throttled |
| `--allow-workload-change` | Do not fail when the workload differs (preset, mix, dataset, access, rate) |
| `--allow-target-change` | Do not fail when the target differs (scheme, bucket/prefix, endpoint, options) |
| `--strict` | Runs of different targets or workloads are an error (exit 2) instead of a warning |
| `--markdown <FILE>` | Write a Markdown summary (PR comment / job summary) |
| `--junit <FILE>` | Write JUnit XML |
| `--json <FILE>` | Write the comparison as JSON |

## `oprobe verify`

Test a finding's advice: replay the run with and without the change (A B A B…) and answer confirmed, refuted or inconclusive

```text
oprobe verify [OPTIONS] <RUNREF> [CODE]
```

Output formats (`-o`): text, json, ndjson, md

| argument | description |
|---|---|
| `<RUNREF>` | The run whose findings to test (RUNREF: id, prefix, last, last~N, label) |
| `<CODE>` | The finding code to verify (default: every finding with a verification) |
| `--all` | Verify every finding that has a verification |
| `--repeat <N>` | Baseline / candidate pairs to run (interleaved A B A B…) · default `3` |
| `--no-calibrate` | Do not store the outcomes or calibrate the capacity history and noise floor |

*Safety*

| argument | description |
|---|---|
| `--dry-run` | Print the plan (requests, bytes, objects written/deleted, cost, ETA) and exit |
| `--read-only` | Refuse every write and delete (exit 5); implied by --existing |
| `--max-cost-usd <USD>` | Stop when the estimated request cost exceeds this (USD; exit 4) |
| `--max-requests <N>` | Stop after this many backend requests (exit 4) |
| `--max-bytes <SIZE>` | Stop after transferring this many bytes, e.g. 10GiB (exit 4) |
| `--max-duration <DURATION>` | Stop after this much wall time, e.g. 5m (exit 4) |
| `--idempotency-key <KEY>` | Name the run prefix after KEY: a retried command reuses and cleans it up |
| `--no-save` | Do not save the replayed runs in the run store |

## `oprobe fix`

Diagnose a target, tune it and verify the recommendation; prints a profile patch

```text
oprobe fix [OPTIONS] [TARGET]
```

Output formats (`-o`): text, json, ndjson, md

*Target*

| argument | description |
|---|---|
| `<TARGET>` | Target name (see `oprobe target list`) or storage URL: s3://bucket/prefix, gcs://bucket, azblob://container, oss://, cos://, b2://, fs:///path, memory:// |
| `-p, --profile <FILE>` | Load a profile (TOML); flags override its values |
| `--endpoint <ENDPOINT>` | Custom endpoint (MinIO, R2, Ceph, private clouds) |
| `--region <REGION>` | Region of the bucket (e.g. us-east-1); most S3-compatible services accept any value |
| `--option <KEY=VALUE>` | Extra backend option, repeatable (e.g. --option enable_virtual_host_style=true) |
| `--anonymous` | Access a public bucket without credentials (s3, gcs, azblob, oss: unsigned requests) |
| `--ca-cert <PEM>` | Trust an extra PEM CA bundle |
| `--insecure` | Skip TLS certificate verification (development only) |
| `--proxy <PROXY>` | Egress proxy URL, or `none` to ignore HTTPS_PROXY/HTTP_PROXY |

*Workload*

| argument | description |
|---|---|
| `--preset <PRESET>` | Workload preset: parquet, checkpoint, small-files, metadata, mixed |
| `-d, --duration <DURATION>` | Measurement window (e.g. 30s, 2m) |
| `--warmup <WARMUP>` | Warmup before measuring (connections, caches) |
| `--max-ops <MAX_OPS>` | Stop after N measured operations |
| `--rate <RATE>` | Open-loop arrival rate (ops/s); latency is measured from the intended start time |
| `--existing <PREFIX>` | Benchmark existing objects under this prefix (read-only) |
| `--objects <OBJECTS>` | Number of dataset objects to generate |
| `--object-size <OBJECT_SIZE>` | Size of each generated object (e.g. 16MiB) |
| `--access <ACCESS>` | Key popularity: uniform, zipf:1.1, hotset:0.2/0.8 |
| `--persist-dataset` | Keep the generated dataset for later runs (oprobe-dataset/<fingerprint>/) |
| `--no-verify` | Skip CRC32C verification |
| `--keep-data` | Do not delete test data when the run ends |

*Client knobs*

| argument | description |
|---|---|
| `-c, --concurrency <CONCURRENCY>` | Concurrent operations (workers) |
| `--io-concurrency <IO_CONCURRENCY>` | Per-operation reader/writer parallelism |
| `--chunk-size <CHUNK_SIZE>` | Reader/writer chunk and multipart part size (e.g. 8MiB) |
| `--range-gap <RANGE_GAP>` | Merge vectored ranges closer than this (e.g. 64KiB) |
| `--max-inflight <MAX_INFLIGHT>` | Cap in-flight HTTP requests (0 = unlimited) |
| `--http <HTTP>` | HTTP version · one of `auto`, `h1`, `h2` |
| `--no-keep-alive` | Open a new connection for every request |
| `--microscope` | Use oprobe's instrumented connection pool instead of OpenDAL's own HTTP client: exact pool queueing, per-dial DNS/TCP/proxy/TLS and HTTP/2 streams, at the cost of measuring a different client than production runs |
| `--cache <SIZE>` | Enable the in-memory read cache with this size (e.g. 512MiB) |
| `--retries <RETRIES>` | Retry attempts for temporary errors |
| `--tail-cut` | Cancel and retry straggler requests (TailCutLayer) |
| `--addressing <STYLE>` | S3 bucket addressing: auto (as configured), virtual (bucket.host) or path (host/bucket) |
| `--checksum <ALGO>` | Checksum computed by the client and verified by the server on writes (S3: crc32c) |
| `--sse <MODE>` | Server-side encryption of written objects (S3: AES256, aws:kms) |

*Cost*

| argument | description |
|---|---|
| `--provider <PROVIDER>` | Pricing preset: aws-s3, gcs, azure-blob, cloudflare-r2, backblaze-b2, aliyun-oss (aliases: aws, gcp, google, azure, r2, b2, oss, aliyun) |
| `--monthly-ops <MONTHLY_OPS>` | Logical operations per month to project costs for |
| `--egress-fraction <EGRESS_FRACTION>` | Fraction of downloads leaving the cloud (0..1) |
| `--stored-gib <STORED_GIB>` | Stored data in GiB |

*SLA (exit code 3 when breached)*

| argument | description |
|---|---|
| `--sla <MODE>` | `none` reports the SLA verdict without failing the command · one of `enforce`, `none` |
| `--max-error-rate <RATE>` | Max share of failed operations, e.g. 1% or 0.01 (default 1%) |
| `--max-throttle-rate <RATE>` | Max share of throttled (429/503) operations, e.g. 0% (default: not checked by `run`; `tune` rejects any throttling) |
| `--p99-ms <MS>` | Max p99 latency per operation in ms (tune rejects trials above it) |

*Output*

| argument | description |
|---|---|
| `--json <FILE>` | Also save the report as JSON (input for `oprobe compare`) |
| `--markdown <FILE>` | Also save a Markdown report |
| `--no-save` | Do not save the run in the run store |
| `--fail-on <FAIL_ON>` | Also exit with code 3 if the diagnosis has findings of this severity or worse (SLA breaches always do, unless `--sla none`) · one of `warning`, `critical` |
| `--label <LABEL>` | Label stored in the report (e.g. a git SHA) |

*Safety*

| argument | description |
|---|---|
| `--dry-run` | Print the plan (requests, bytes, objects written/deleted, cost, ETA) and exit |
| `--read-only` | Refuse every write and delete (exit 5); implied by --existing |
| `--max-cost-usd <USD>` | Stop when the estimated request cost exceeds this (USD; exit 4) |
| `--max-requests <N>` | Stop after this many backend requests (exit 4) |
| `--max-bytes <SIZE>` | Stop after transferring this many bytes, e.g. 10GiB (exit 4) |
| `--max-duration <DURATION>` | Stop after this much wall time, e.g. 5m (exit 4) |
| `--idempotency-key <KEY>` | Name the run prefix after KEY: a retried command reuses and cleans it up |

*Tuning*

| argument | description |
|---|---|
| `--objective <OBJECTIVE>` | What to optimize · one of `goodput`, `p99`, `cost`, `balanced` · default `goodput` |
| `--trial-duration <TRIAL_DURATION>` | Measurement window per trial · default `5s` |
| `--trial-warmup <TRIAL_WARMUP>` | Warmup per trial · default `1s` |
| `--max-trials <MAX_TRIALS>` | Maximum number of trials · default `24` |
| `--max-concurrency <MAX_CONCURRENCY>` | Highest concurrency to try · default `256` |
| `--cooldown <COOLDOWN>` | Pause after a throttled trial · default `5s` |
| `--max-throttle-ratio <RATIO>` | Share of throttled requests a configuration may cause and still be feasible (default 0.001, or the profile's `sla.max_throttle_rate`) |
| `--boundary-repeats <BOUNDARY_REPEATS>` | Runs of each bisection trial near the throttle boundary · default `2` |
| `--headroom-ratio <RATIO>` | In-flight headroom kept below the throttling ceiling (default 0.15) |
| `--budget <DURATION>` | Total wall-time budget of the tuning step, e.g. 5m (caps the trials so the estimate fits) |

*Verification*

| argument | description |
|---|---|
| `--repeat <N>` | Baseline / candidate pairs of the verification · default `2` |
| `--write-profile <FILE>` | Write the recommended profile (TOML) to this file |

*Replay*

| argument | description |
|---|---|
| `--from <RUNREF>` | Fix the workload of a stored run (RUNREF): its spec, with credentials resolved again from the target; other flags and --set override it (as `run --from`) |
| `--set <KEY=VALUE>` | Override one setting of the workload, repeatable (as `run --set`) |

## `oprobe runs`

Saved runs: list, show, open, export, rm, gc

```text
oprobe runs [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>
```

## `oprobe runs list`

List saved runs, newest first

```text
oprobe runs list [OPTIONS]
```

Output formats (`-o`): text, json, ndjson, md

| argument | description |
|---|---|
| `-n, --limit <LIMIT>` | Show at most N runs · default `20` |

## `oprobe runs show`

Show a run's full report (-o md|html|json for documents)

```text
oprobe runs show [OPTIONS] [RUNREF]
```

Output formats (`-o`): text, json, ndjson, md, html

| argument | description |
|---|---|
| `<RUNREF>` | Run id, id prefix, `last`, `last~N`, label, or path to a .oprobe / report .json file · default `last` |
| `--detail` | Every column, per-stage and per-verb breakdowns, the timeline and the 5 slowest operations |

## `oprobe runs open`

Open a run in the app (native window)

```text
oprobe runs open [OPTIONS] <RUNREF>
```

Output formats (`-o`): text, json, ndjson

| argument | description |
|---|---|
| `<RUNREF>` | Run id, id prefix, `last`, `last~N`, label, or path to a .oprobe / report .json file |

## `oprobe runs export`

Export a run (html, md, json, ndjson, csv, har, otlp)

```text
oprobe runs export [OPTIONS] --format <FORMAT> <RUNREF>
```

Output formats (`-o`): text, json, ndjson

| argument | description |
|---|---|
| `<RUNREF>` | Run id, id prefix, `last`, `last~N`, label, or path to a .oprobe file |
| `-f, --format <FORMAT>` | Export format · one of `json`, `ndjson`, `csv`, `har`, `otlp`, `md`, `html` |
| `--out <PATH>` | Write to this file (default: stdout) |
| `--endpoint <URL>` | OTLP/HTTP collector to push to (e.g. http://localhost:4318); with --format otlp |
| `--table <TABLE>` | CSV rows: requests or ops · default `requests` |
| `--signal <SIGNAL>` | OTLP signal: one OTLP/JSON document per signal; `all` needs --out DIR (two files) or --endpoint (posts /v1/traces and /v1/metrics) · one of `traces`, `metrics`, `all` · default `traces` |

|---|---|

## `oprobe runs gc`

Delete old runs (keeps the newest and every baseline run)

```text
oprobe runs gc [OPTIONS]
```

Output formats (`-o`): text, json, ndjson

| argument | description |
|---|---|
| `--keep <KEEP>` | Keep the newest N runs · default `50` |
| `--older-than <DURATION>` | Only delete runs older than this, e.g. 30d, 12h, 2w |
| `--dry-run` | Show what would be deleted |

## `oprobe analyze`

Re-slice a run by API, connection, remote, stage or second

```text
oprobe analyze [OPTIONS] [RUNREF]
```

Output formats (`-o`): text, json, ndjson

| argument | description |
|---|---|
| `<RUNREF>` | Run id, id prefix, `last`, `last~N`, label, or path to a .oprobe file · default `last` |
| `--by <KEY>` | Group requests by: api, conn, remote, stage, second, status |
| `--window <A..B>` | Only requests started in this window, seconds from the window start (e.g. 5..10) |
| `--where <K=V,…>` | Only requests matching all conditions, e.g. api=GetObject,status=503 (repeatable) |
| `--slowest <PCT>` | Attribute the slowest PCT percent of the (filtered) requests (default 1) |

## `oprobe explain`

Narrate a run's causes and advice, or document a finding code

```text
oprobe explain [OPTIONS] [RUNREF|FINDING_CODE]
```

Output formats (`-o`): text, json, ndjson, md

| argument | description |
|---|---|
| `<RUNREF\|FINDING_CODE>` | A RUNREF (id, prefix, `last`, `last~N`, label, .oprobe path) or a finding code (e.g. `throttling`); `oprobe explain --list` lists the codes |
| `--list` | List every finding code |
| `--top <TOP>` | Findings to narrate for a run · default `3` |

## `oprobe doctor`

Check endpoint reachability, TLS, clock skew, credentials and permissions

```text
oprobe doctor [OPTIONS] [TARGET]
```

Output formats (`-o`): text, json, ndjson

*Target*

| argument | description |
|---|---|
| `<TARGET>` | Target name (see `oprobe target list`) or storage URL: s3://bucket/prefix, gcs://bucket, azblob://container, oss://, cos://, b2://, fs:///path, memory:// |
| `-p, --profile <FILE>` | Load a profile (TOML); flags override its values |
| `--endpoint <ENDPOINT>` | Custom endpoint (MinIO, R2, Ceph, private clouds) |
| `--region <REGION>` | Region of the bucket (e.g. us-east-1); most S3-compatible services accept any value |
| `--option <KEY=VALUE>` | Extra backend option, repeatable (e.g. --option enable_virtual_host_style=true) |
| `--anonymous` | Access a public bucket without credentials (s3, gcs, azblob, oss: unsigned requests) |
| `--ca-cert <PEM>` | Trust an extra PEM CA bundle |
| `--insecure` | Skip TLS certificate verification (development only) |
| `--proxy <PROXY>` | Egress proxy URL, or `none` to ignore HTTPS_PROXY/HTTP_PROXY |
| `--read-only` | Only check reachability and listing; never write (the default; kept for scripts) |
| `--write-probe` | Also write, read back, stat and delete a 256 KiB probe object under `oprobe-run-<time>-doctor/` (the default is read-only) |
| `-v, --verbose` | Show the raw backend error of failed checks |

## `oprobe probe`

Measure DNS / TCP / proxy / TLS handshakes and cold vs warm TTFB of an endpoint
